messages:
carmen: Hi all  I'm about to open my first PR touching runtime scheduling + a small formatter change. Quick questions before I push: do we allow merge commits or always squash? any branch protection rules I should be aware of?

drew: Welcome! We enforce 'Squash and merge' on the repo. No merge commits. Also branch protection requires: passing CI, 1 approval from CODEOWNERS (2 if it touches api/public), and no direct pushes to main.

kai: For branch names use `user/<name>/short-desc` for non-urgent work (eg user/carmen/sched-tweak). For backports use `release/<semver>-patch` and PRs should target release branches directly.

carmen: Got it. For commits: is it okay to keep multiple commits during development and then squash at merge? Or should I rebase interactively first?

drew: Both are fine. Typical flow: develop with multiple commits, then either squash via GitHub's squash-on-merge or do an interactive rebase to craft the final commit message if you want a cleaner history. If you rebase, force-push with --force-with-lease.

kai: Our CI also checks commit message format. We use Conventional Commits. Example commit to copy:

```
fix(runtime): tighten scheduling window for short-lived tasks

This reduces task starvation under high concurrency. Unit + integration tests included.
Resolves: #912
```

qa-bot: qa-bot: please add a `how to test` section to the PR body; link any smoke scripts. See https://docs.redwood.ai/dev/pr-guides

carmen: Where's the STYLE.md/contributing? I searched root but couldn't find it in this repo.

drew: It was moved into docs/ in runtime repo: docs/CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md. There are language-specific lint hooks configured in .github/workflows.

kai: A few runtime-specific things to watch: if you touch hot paths include a perf microbenchmark in perf/benchmarks and reference results in the PR. We prefer diffs that are easy to review; split big refactors into a rename-only PR then a behavior PR.

carmen: If my PR touches config defaults, do I need to update ops runbooks?

drew: Yes — add a short note in ops/CHANGELOG.md and if it affects customers mention it in the PR under 'Rollout & Monitoring'. If it's risky, add a rollout plan and Canary gates.

kai: For urgent reviews, ping @drew or add the `expedite-review` label (oncall will triage). Don't ping multiple people in a row — use the label + short summary.

carmen: Any conventions for binary files or proto changes?
drew: Protos: always generate and include the generated files, and add a compat note if breaking. Binaries: avoid committing large binaries; put them in assets/ and use git-lfs only when approved by infra.

qa-bot: Also run `pre-commit run --all-files` and `pytest tests/unit -q` locally. Perf tests: `python perf/run.py --quick` for a smoke run.

carmen: Nice, I'll run the hooks and add the perf sketch. One last: PR template has a checklist right?

kai: Yes, the template auto-adds a checklist: changelog, tests, CI, reviewers, rollout. Fill them out. If you want a second pair for a perf patch ask for a perf-review in the PR.

carmen: Thanks team! I'll open a draft PR first and invite reviewers. :raised_hands:

drew: Happy to review the draft. :eyes:
